usamts-2007-r3-01.prompt: We construct a sculpture consisting of infinitely many cubes, as follows. Start with a cube with side length 1. Then, at the center of each face, attach a cube with side length $\frac13$ (so that the center of a face of each attached cube is the center of a face of the original cube). Continue this procedure indefinitely: at the center of each exposed face of a cube in the structure, attach (in the same fashion) a smaller cube with side length one-third that of the exposed face. What is the volume of the entire sculpture?

usamts-2007-r3-02.prompt:
Gene starts with the $3\times 3$ grid of 0's shown at left below. He then repeatedly chooses a $2\times 2$ square within the grid and increases all four numbers in the chosen $2\times 2$ square by 1. One possibility for Gene's first three steps is shown below.
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 0&0&0\\\hline 0&0&0\\\hline 0&0&0\\\hline\end{array}\ \to\ \begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 0&0&0\\\hline 1&1&0\\\hline 1&1&0\\\hline\end{array}\ \to\ \begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 0&1&1\\\hline 1&2&1\\\hline 1&1&0\\\hline\end{array}\ \to\ \begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 0&1&1\\\hline 2&3&1\\\hline 2&2&0\\\hline\end{array}$$
How many different grids can be produced with this method such that each box contains an integer from 1 to 12, inclusive? (The numbers in the boxes need not be distinct.)

usamts-2007-r3-03.prompt: Consider all polynomials $f(x)$ with integer coefficients such that $f(200) = f(7) = 2007$ and $0 < f(0) < 2007$. Show that the value of $f(0)$ does not depend on the choice of polynomial, and find $f(0)$.

usamts-2007-r3-04.prompt:
Prove that $101$ divides infinitely many of the numbers in the set
$$\{2007,\ 20072007,\ 200720072007,\ 2007200720072007,\ \dots\}.$$
usamts-2007-r3-04.answer: Since $10^4 \equiv 1 \pmod{101}$, the number made of $n$ blocks "2007" is $\equiv 2007n \equiv 88n \pmod{101}$; it is divisible by $101$ whenever $101 \mid n$.

usamts-2007-r3-05.prompt:
For every rational number $0 < \frac pq < 1$, where $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime, construct a circle with center $\left(\frac pq, \frac{1}{2q^2}\right)$ and diameter $\frac{1}{q^2}$. Also construct circles centered at $\left(0, \frac12\right)$ and $\left(1, \frac12\right)$ with diameter 1.

(a) Prove that any two such circles intersect in at most 1 point.

(b) Prove that the total area of all of the circles is
$$\frac{\pi}{4}\left(1 + \frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^\infty \frac{1}{i^3}}{\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^\infty\frac{1}{i^4}}\right).$$
usamts-2007-r3-05.answer: (a) For circles at $\frac{r_1}{s_1} \neq \frac{r_2}{s_2}$ (both tangent to the $x$-axis from above), $d^2 - (\rho_1 + \rho_2)^2 = \frac{(r_1s_2 - r_2s_1)^2 - 1}{s_1^2s_2^2} \ge 0$, so they never cross. (b) Count the pairs $0 \le a \le b$ with weight $\frac1{b^4}$ in two ways: $\sum_b \frac{b+1}{b^4} = \left(\sum_{(r,s)} \frac{1}{s^4}\right)\sum_n \frac1{n^4}$.
